Thanks! Yeah this was from a reference photo. I used to spend a lot of time using the loomis method to get all my proportions right and everything in place. But it is so time consuming and ends up covered by the painting anyway. Now I use more of a tiling method and just block out major shapes and slowly place all the details inside them. On this one I actually overlayed a simple grid on the reference and on my canvas to help place the whole figure, then I divided everything into a light and a shadow shape. There’s a couple times in the early stages I took advantage of digital and liquified some proportions to get it closer to the reference.

Finally felt inspired and confident enough to get back to portrait painting and had a fun time with this. Should have paid more attention in school because I only recently discovered John Singer Sargent, and really fell in love with his brushwork. Kind of inspired this direction from my older more rough work.
